Clean pass with two disclosed caveats. (1) Administered language: the test was given one-on-one in Bangla; no Bangla instrument exists in the Dataverse deposit (data + do-files only) or in the IZA DP 15920 / J-PAL WP4445 appendices, so the shipped item_text is the authors' English from appendix Table A4 with language=Bengali and no _translated columns (text_source=translated_substitute fallback). (2) Each of the 15 questions has three grade-level variants and the IRW table carries no grade column, so item_text concatenates the Level 1 / Level 2 / Level 3 wordings. Mapping VERIFIED: live per-item proportion correct matches appendix Table B3's total-sample column at 2 dp for all 15 items and the per-item marks recovered from the .dta match Table B3's 'Marks assigned' column exactly. No dictionary problem found: metadata Description 'Academic achievement in an RCT' and the table's live content agree (Step 3b check passed). || ORCHESTRATOR (Step 5b, batch_040). VERIFIED status UPHELD against lint_verification's WARN ('VERIFIED but its evidence hedges'). The hedge is about which GRADE-LEVEL VARIANT (Level 1/2/3) a child received -- a fact the table cannot carry because it has no grade column -- not about item identity. Every item IS distinguished from every other by the (proportion, marks) pair, which is what VERIFIED requires, so the status is correct and the WARN is a false positive on the phrase 'does NOT establish'. Independently re-checked the underlying numbers on the live table: per-item proportion correct reproduces the agent's reported values with max |difference| = 0.0000 across all 15 items (0.92, 0.76, 0.67, 0.57, 0.63, 0.35, 0.61, 0.67, 0.68, 0.41, 0.82, 0.84, 0.72, 0.45, 0.65), and the e1_item3/e1_item8 tie at 0.67 is real, confirming that the marks column is genuinely load-bearing for those two. Unincorporated: the sheet1_sweep_2026-09-03.csv row for this table reads 'see slack discussion', which the agent could not access -- if that recorded a prior decision, it is not reflected here.

Clean pass with two caveats. (1) Recall period: the shipped item_text and instructions are Cohen's own PSS-10 form verbatim ("In the last month..."), but Gillman et al. state the measure "assessed individual's feelings and thoughts during the most stressful event identified in the last three months" -- the administered recall frame differs from the canonical wording shipped, and the study does not print its modified wording. (2) Reverse-scoring: PS_4_R/PS_5_R/PS_7_R/PS_8_R are stored RAW, not reverse-scored, so the 0-4 Never..Very Often anchors apply as written to every item. Verified in-data: those four correlate -0.09 to -0.37 with the six negatively-worded items and +0.47 to +0.55 among themselves, and the unreversed 10-item alpha is 0.673, reproducing the paper's reported alpha = .67 (properly reverse-keyed it is 0.864) -- i.e. the study's own reported PSS reliability, and the source .sav's PS_Total column (= the plain unreversed sum, exact for 397/412 rows), were computed without reversing. (3) Rights check: the PSS is free for non-profit research/educational use per Cohen's lab FAQ ("YES, if it's for research or educational (non-profit) purposes"); a fee applies only to "profit making ventures", and the full instrument is published openly on the lab's own site -- no blocking clause. || ORCHESTRATOR (Step 5b, batch_040). CONFIRMED independently, and the numbers are worth stating exactly because this claim is a defect finding about the SOURCE PAPER's analysis, not about the IRW table. On the live table (404 complete cases): alpha computed on the items AS STORED, with no reversal, is 0.67 -- reproducing Gillman et al.'s reported alpha of .67 to the published 2 dp -- while properly keyed alpha is 0.86. The paper's reliability figure was therefore computed without reverse-scoring items 4/5/7/8. Polarity confirmed too: all 24 correlations between the four _R items and the six negatively-worded items are negative (-0.093 to -0.371), with no sign exceptions. This is a defect in the source paper's analysis; the IRW table itself is correct and the itemtext ships accordingly.

Clean pass with caveats. (1) LANGUAGE: the study administered the PHQ-9 in Amharic (paper: "The questionnaire was developed in English and then translated into Amharic"; "Data were collected by trained interviewers using the local language, Amharic"), but the deposit (PeerJ supplementary peerj-11-15053-s001.dta, via Europe PMC PMC10100826 supplementaryFiles) contains zero Ethiopic characters across all 26 variable labels and all 8 value-label sets, and the paper reproduces no items. Fallback per the schema: English in the base fields, language=Amharic, _translated columns empty, text_source=translated_substitute. (2) The .dta variable labels tie PHQ1..PHQ9 to abbreviated symptom mnemonics in canonical PHQ-9 order (e.g. PHQ6 = "R1 Feeling bad about self", PHQ9 = "R1 Thoughts of being better off dead"), which fixes the code->item mapping; the shipped words are the fuller canonical English PHQ-9 wording rather than those abbreviations, and the "R1" wave prefix in the labels was not carried over. (3) The .dta has no value labels for the PHQ columns, so the 0-3 anchors are canonical (Not at all / Several days / More than half the days / Nearly every day), corroborated by the paper: "Each item was scored on a four-point Likert scale, 0/not at all to 3/nearly every day." (4) PHQ9 (suicidal ideation) is observed only at resp 0-2 in the live table (no respondent used 3); the resp=3 option row is shipped for it anyway because the scale ran 0-3 for every item. (5) Rights: no fee, non-commercial or no-redistribution clause could be quoted for the PHQ-9; the wording was copied from the CC BY 4.0 PeerJ deposit and the canonical instrument, and PHQ-9 tables have shipped before (bitew_2020_phq9, same instrument, same country, same fallback). RETRY TEST: n/a, not a block. || ORCHESTRATOR (Step 5b, batch_040). CONFIRMED independently on the live table. The agent's corroborating claim holds EXACTLY: PHQ9 is the only one of the nine items never observed at resp=3 (range 0-2; every other item reaches 3, with counts of 3s ranging 3 to 21), and the endorsement ordering matches the paper's text -- PHQ4 most endorsed (mean 0.548) and PHQ9 (suicidal ideation) least (mean 0.061), with PHQ3 and PHQ1 next after PHQ4. The resp=3 option row is still shipped for PHQ9, correctly: the scale ran 0-3 for every item and an unused level is a property of the responses, not of the instrument.
